audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for labor grievance, servant leadership, generational stereotyping, masculinity and sexualized threat, violent coercion, providence language, worker revolt, Adoram's death, civil-war mobilization, prophetic de-escalation, religious centralization, golden calves, priestly class, and political fear.

verses.restored: Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel came to Shechem to make him king.

familiar.text: And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king.

modern.text: Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had gone there to make him king.

verses.restored: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard—while still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon and lived—

modern.text: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about this, he was still in Egypt where he had fled from King Solomon and had been living ever since.

modern.text: So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and the whole assembly of Israel came to Rehoboam and said,

verses.restored: Your father made our yoke hard. Now lighten hard service of your father and heavy yoke he placed upon us, and we will serve you.

familiar.text: Thy father made our yoke grievous: now therefore make thou the grievous service of thy father, and his heavy yoke which he put upon us, lighter, and we will serve thee.

modern.text: “Your father put a heavy yoke on us. But now you should lighten the burden of your father’s service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”

verses.restored: He said, Go for three days, then return to me. The people went.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Depart yet for three days, then come again to me. And the people departed.

modern.text: Rehoboam answered, “Go away for three days and then return to me.” So the people departed.

verses.restored: King Rehoboam consulted elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he lived, saying, How do you counsel me to answer this people?

familiar.text: And king Rehoboam consulted with the old men, that stood before Solomon his father while he yet lived, and said, How do ye advise that I may answer this people?

modern.text: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. “How do you advise me to respond to these people?” he asked.

verses.restored: They spoke to him, If today you become servant to this people, serve them, answer them, and speak good words, they will be your servants all days.

familiar.text: And they spake unto him, saying, If thou wilt be a servant unto this people this day, and wilt serve them, and answer them, and speak good words to them, then they will be thy servants for ever.

modern.text: They replied, “If you will be a servant to these people and serve them this day, and if you will respond by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”

familiar.text: But he forsook the counsel of the old men, which they had given him, and consulted with the young men that were grown up with him, and which stood before him:

modern.text: But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders; instead, he consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him.

original.text: וַֽיַּעֲזֹ֛ב אֶת עֲצַ֥ת הַזְּקֵנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְעָצֻ֑הוּ וַיִּוָּעַ֗ץ אֶת הַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר גָּדְל֣וּ אִתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָעֹמְדִ֖ים לְפָנָֽיו

verses.restored: He said to them, What counsel do you give, that we may answer this people who said, Lighten yoke your father placed upon us?

familiar.text: And he said unto them, What counsel give ye that we may answer this people, who have spoken to me, saying, Make the yoke which thy father did put upon us lighter?

modern.text: He asked them, “What message do you advise that we send back to these people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”

verses.restored: Young men who grew with him said, Thus say to this people: My father made your yoke heavy, but you say, Lighten it. Thus say: My little finger is thicker than my father's loins.

familiar.text: And the young men that were grown up with him spake unto him, saying, Thus shalt thou speak unto this people that spake unto thee, saying, Thy father made our yoke heavy, but make thou it lighter unto us; thus shalt thou say unto them, My little finger shall be thicker than my father’s loins.

modern.text: The young men who had grown up with him replied, “This is how you should answer these people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you should make it lighter.’ This is what you should tell them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!

familiar.text: And now whereas my father did lade you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke: my father hath chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.

modern.text: Whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.’”

modern.text: After three days, Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, since the king had said, “Come back to me on the third day.”

modern.text: and spoke to them as the young men had advised, saying, “Whereas my father made your yoke heavy, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.”

modern.text: So the king did not listen to the people, and indeed this turn of events was from the LORD, to fulfill the word He had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah the Shilonite. The Kingdom Divided (2 Chronicles 10:16–19)

verses.restored: All Israel saw king did not listen. People answered king: What portion have we in David? No inheritance in son of Jesse. To your tents, Israel. Now see to your own house, David. Israel went to their tents.

familiar.text: So when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David. So Israel departed unto their tents.

modern.text: When all Israel saw that the king had refused to listen to them, they answered the king: “What portion do we have in David, and what inheritance in the son of Jesse? To your tents, O Israel! Look now to your own house, O David!” So the Israelites went home,

modern.text: Then King Rehoboam sent out Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam mounted his chariot in haste and escaped to Jerusalem.

translation_notes: The northern assembly's complaint is a labor and taxation grievance: Solomon's service and yoke were heavy. The kingdom divides after the new ruler refuses material relief.
The elders advise servant leadership, but their phrase that the people will then be servants forever still reflects hierarchy rather than democratic equality.
The problem is not that advisors are young. It is that Rehoboam chooses peers insulated by privilege who recommend humiliation and intensified coercion.
The little-finger/loins boast and scorpion threat are sexualized masculinity and torture rhetoric. They should not be admired as strength.
Providence language in verse 15 does not erase Rehoboam's deliberate refusal, advisor responsibility, or the people's valid grievance.
Adoram is killed as the official embodiment of forced labor. Worker revolt does not make mob killing harmless, and his death does not erase the system he administered.
The word through Shemaiah stops a civil war between kin. Divine speech functions here as de-escalation rather than battle authorization.
Jeroboam's fear of losing political loyalty leads him to redesign worship. Accessibility concerns about traveling to Jerusalem are real, but they are manipulated to secure his throne.
Calling non-Levite priests 'from the lowest people' in some translations reinforces class contempt. The Hebrew more likely means from the whole/ends of the people.
The critique of Bethel and Dan must not become contempt for later Samaritans, present-day religious minorities, or non-centralized worship.
safety_note: Center the workers' demand to lighten the yoke. Do not glorify authoritarian masculinity, torture threats, mob killing, civil war, or religious monopoly. Providence does not cancel human accountability, and accessible worship must not be manipulated for regime security.
